goal: v0.2.0: live probe mode and a GitHub Action, built behind a security gate that every iteration must pass.
gate: bash scripts/verify.sh (typecheck, tests, build, 11-check security audit). Run by scripts/ralph/ralph.sh itself; cannot be changed from this file.
acceptanceCriteria: bash scripts/verify.sh exits 0 after every iteration, including all 11 security audit checks
No file under the protected paths (scripts/verify.sh, scripts/security-audit.mjs, security/, scripts/ralph/, .claude/, .github/workflows/) changes; ralph.sh halts the run if one does
Every automatable task below has passes: true, each landed as its own commit
No new production dependency; any new dev dependency is justified in plans/progress.md
plans/progress.md records what each task changed and learned
securityRequirements: Network access only from src/core/load.ts and src/probe/ (enforced by the audit)
The probe sends only GET, HEAD and OPTIONS, never to private or loopback addresses by default, and never forwards credentials to a host other than the declared server
Secrets come only from environment variables and never appear in any output, report, log or error
Workflows and action.yml pin every action to a commit SHA, declare least-privilege permissions, and never interpolate untrusted ${{ }} values into shell commands

features.title: Polish report wording: singular counts and required-vs-recommended metadata
acceptanceCriteria: No rule message or finding produced for any fixture in fixtures/ contains the text "(s)" or "All 1 "; a test renders every fixture and asserts this
META001's message states required and recommended gaps separately, e.g. "1 required field missing, 1 recommended", and a test covers it
Existing tests updated rather than deleted; total test count does not drop
bash scripts/verify.sh passes
features.notes: Warm-up task. Seen on the Petstore run: 'All 1 high-impact action(s)' and '1 required listing field(s) missing' while listing two items.

features.title: Safe HTTP client for probing (src/probe/http.ts)
acceptanceCriteria: safeRequest(url, options) is built on node:http/node:https with a custom DNS lookup that rejects loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, unspecified and IPv4-mapped IPv6 private addresses AFTER resolution, so DNS rebinding cannot reach internal hosts
Methods other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS throw before any socket opens
Redirects are followed manually, at most 3, re-validating scheme and resolved address on every hop; any credential header is dropped when the origin changes
Default total timeout 10s and default body cap 1 MiB; oversize bodies are aborted and flagged truncated
HTTPS only by default; plain HTTP and private networks need explicit options (allowInsecureHttp, allowPrivateNetwork) that default to false
Sends User-Agent muse-ready/<version>
test/probe.security.test.ts exists and contains every test title listed under probeSecurityTests in security/policy.json, verbatim, each exercising real behaviour against local test servers
No new production dependency
bash scripts/verify.sh passes
features.notes: The audit starts enforcing the probe security tests the moment src/probe/ exists, so create the test file in the same commit. 'never writes credentials into any report format' can assert on safeRequest results and errors for now; T-004 extends it to reports.

features.title: --probe mode with live checks NET002, LAT001, ERR002, PAGE002
acceptanceCriteria: CLI flag --probe is off by default; without it the tool opens no connection except fetching a URL spec (a test asserts the probe module is never called)
Probe target is the first declared OpenAPI server, or connector.serverUrl for MCP input

The probe only calls GET/HEAD/OPTIONS operations that need no required parameters (or whose required parameters have a default or example); a test runs a full probe against a local server exposing write operations and asserts it received zero POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE requests

Each new rule lives in its own file under src/rules/ with a rationale and is marked provisional where Muse's limits are undocumented: NET002 (DNS resolves to public addresses and TLS verifies), LAT001 (p95 latency across up to 5 GETs; warn above 3s, fail above 30s or timeout), ERR002 (unauthenticated call to a secured operation returns 401/403 and the body contains no stack trace or secret-looking strings), PAGE002 (sampled list response under 1 MiB; warn above 256 KiB)
Each new rule has a passing and a failing case in tests using local servers
Probe rules return not-applicable when --probe is off
The JSON report gains probe: { enabled, target, requests: [{ method, path, status, ms }] } and the terminal, Markdown and SARIF outputs show probe findings
README documents --probe, exactly what traffic it sends, and the regenerated rule catalog (node scripts/rules-doc.mjs)
bash scripts/verify.sh passes

features.title: Authenticated probing via MUSE_READY_TOKEN
acceptanceCriteria: The token is read only from the MUSE_READY_TOKEN environment variable, never from a CLI argument or config file
Header defaults to 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'; config probe.authHeader can switch to an API-key header name
The token is sent only to the exact origin of the probe target, never to the spec host if different and never across a redirect to another origin (tests)
A test runs a full probe with a known token and asserts the token string appears in none of: terminal output, JSON, Markdown, SARIF, badge, thrown errors
bash scripts/verify.sh passes

features.title: JavaScript GitHub Action (action.yml at repo root)
acceptanceCriteria: action.yml uses runs.using: node24 with main pointing at a committed, bundled action/dist/index.js
Inputs: spec (required), config, fail-under, probe (default false), sarif-file (default muse-ready.sarif), badge-file. Outputs: score, grade, passed, sarif-file
Writes the Markdown report to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and the SARIF file to disk; sets outputs via $GITHUB_OUTPUT using a random heredoc delimiter so values cannot inject extra outputs
Makes no GitHub API calls and needs no token; the action's source lives under src/action/ and passes the audit's network invariant
No new production dependency; a bundler may be added as a dev dependency only if its install script is already allowed by security/policy.json (esbuild is)
A test runs the bundled entry with fake INPUT_* and GITHUB_* environment variables and temp files, and asserts outputs, step summary and SARIF
A test fails if action/dist/index.js is stale relative to the source
The audit's workflow-hardening check passes for action.yml
bash scripts/verify.sh passes
features.notes: action/ is not part of the npm package; the audit's package-contents check will confirm that.

features.title: Example workflow and Action docs
acceptanceCriteria: docs/examples/muse-ready.yml: triggers on pull_request (never pull_request_target), top-level permissions contents: read plus security-events: write only on the job that uploads SARIF, every uses: pinned to a 40-character SHA with a version comment, persist-credentials: false on checkout
Uses actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 (v7.0.1) and github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@1c5b675653bb5c22dbe9b12b556ec555138e09fd (v4.38.1)
A test parses the example with the yaml package and asserts the pinning, permissions and trigger rules above
README gains a GitHub Action section with the snippet and a one-paragraph explanation of the permissions it needs and why
bash scripts/verify.sh passes
features.notes: Depends on T-005. Do not add files under .github/workflows/ (protected).

features.title: Opt-in PR comment from the Action
acceptanceCriteria: Human decision required first
features.skipReason: Needs a human decision: posting comments requires pull-requests: write and GitHub API calls from the action, which widens the token's permissions and the network surface.
